newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to import 600,000 tonnes more wheat.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to import 600,000 tonnes more wheat.

text.p: The Pakistani government decided on Sunday to import 600,000 more tonnes of wheat to stabilise domestic prices, an official statement said Sunday.
Last week, the Food and Agriculture Ministry bought 270,000 tonnes of wheat from U.S. and Australian suppliers for shipment by January 31.

A meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee of caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's cabinet on Sunday "approved the import of additional 0.60 million tonnes of wheat to stabilise the prices in the market," the government statement said.
A Food and Agriculture Ministry official said last week Islamabad was likely to increase its wheat import target for fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) to 2.3 million tonnes from 1.8 million tonnes.
Pakistan has produced 17 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 compared to 17.57 million tonnes in 1995/96, when it imported 1.9 million tonnes from the United States and Australia.
